title: Can you find an angle in a picture and name its vertex?
description: In the picture of a bicycle, two parts meet at a point. They are drawn as two rays from that point, and the point is named as the vertex. A last check writes the angle with the vertex as the middle letter.
teaching_notes: One idea: an angle in a picture is found where two parts meet at a point, and the two parts become the arms. Watch for students who write the vertex letter first or last in the name of the angle.

source: Can you find the angles in the given pictures? Draw the rays forming any one of the angles and name the vertex of the angle.
video_script.why: The child finds two parts that meet at a point in a picture, draws them as the two arms, and names the vertex and the angle.
video_script.substitution: Draw the two parts of the picture that meet at a point as rays from that point.
video_script.anchor: a picture of a bicycle with the points A, B, C and D marked on it, shown with a wooden crate, a ladder and a bridge
video_script.payoff_line: The arms are the rays D B and D C, and the vertex is D

final_answer.value: In the bicycle, angle BDC has the arms DB and DC, and its vertex is D
final_answer.spoken: in the bicycle, one angle is B D C. The arms are the rays D B and D C, and the vertex is D

never_show: the vertex letter of the chosen angle, before the answer beat
maths_rules: An angle in a picture is found where two parts meet at a point.
The two parts are drawn as rays, DB and DC, and they are the arms of the angle.
Both rays start at D, so D is the vertex.
The vertex is always the middle letter in the name, so the angle is BDC, or CDB.
video_script.design: One idea: two parts that meet at a point make an angle with that point as the vertex. The bicycle stays on the board and the two parts light up. The method is the same way as the examples in the book on the angle made by a book cover.
open_questions: The pictures are not visible in the extracted text. The worklist answer takes the bicycle, with the angle BDC at the point D, as an example, and any angle is a valid answer. Please confirm the letters against the printed picture.
